question:
**Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:**

Neither the projection of growth nor the estimation of deficit trends (1)/ appear to have accounted for the liquidity constraints (2)/ that small-scale enterprises face (3)/ during cyclical downturns in demand. (4)
solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. appear to have accounted .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in part **(2)** of the sentence: *appear to have accounted.*
 
• The subject of the sentence, **Neither the projection of growth nor the estimation of deficit trends**, is singular.
 
• When two subjects are joined by **"neither...nor,"** the verb agrees with the nearest subject, which in this case is singular (**estimation of deficit trends**).
 
• Therefore, the verb should be in singular form: **"appears" instead of "appear."**

Correct sentence: *Neither the projection of growth nor the estimation of deficit trends **appears** to have accounted for the liquidity constraints that small-scale enterprises face during cyclical downturns in demand.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement Rules:**

 
 
• When two subjects are joined by **"neither...nor,"** the verb agrees with the subject closest to it.
 
• For example: *Neither the students nor the teacher **was** present.*
 
 
 
• **Common Errors in Subject-Verb Agreement:**
 
 
• Confusion with collective nouns, compound subjects, or phrases that separate the subject from the verb.
 
• Ensure the verb corresponds to the actual subject, not a nearby noun or phrase.
